steps.description:
Write a function named increase(num) with an input argument num. It will decrease num by 5 and returns the result.

Test your function by calling it with the following input arguments and saving each result to a variable: result1 = increase(100) result2 = increase(-5) result3 = increase(0) Display the value of each variable.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

95 -10 -5

Write a function named multiply(x, y) that takes in 2 integers x and y. It will calculate the product of x and y (multiplication) and return the result.

Write a program that asks the user to input the 2 integers in a row and call your function to perform the multiplication. It will then display the returned result.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 4 3

12 -20

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 integers: 4 3 12

Example 2 Input 2 integers: 12 -20 -240

Write a function named scoring(score1, score2) that takes in 2 integers as the scores of 2 subjects. It will calculate the total and average and return the 2 values.

Write a program that asks the user to input 2 scores in a row and call your function to perform the calculations. It will then display returned results.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 74 83

92 60

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 scores: 74 83 total 157 average 78.5

Example 2 Input 2 scores: 92 60 total 152 average 76.0

Write a function named scoring(scorelist) that takes in a list of scores. It will calculate the total score and return the result.

Write a program that asks the user to input a list of scores (as floats) in a row and call your function to perform the calculation. It will then display the returned results.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 70 83 90 60.5

49 44 53

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input scores: 70 83 90 60.5 total 303.5

Example 2 Input scores: 49 44 53 total 146.0

Write a function named scoring(scorelist) that takes in a list of scores. It will calculate the average score rounded to the whole number and return the result.

Write a program that asks the user to input a list of scores (as floats) in a row and call your function to perform the calculation. It will then display the returned results.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 70 83 90 60.5

49 44 53

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Input scores: 70 83 90 60.5 average 76 Example 2 Input scores: 49 44 53 average 49

Write a function named scoring(scorelist) that takes in a list of scores. It will perform the following: 1. Calculate the average scores rounded to whole number. 2. The grade is determined as follow: "distinction" for average more than 75 "moderate" for average from 50 to 75 "fail" for average less than 50 3. Return the average and grade.

Write a program that asks the user to input a list of scores in a row and call your function to perform the calculations. It will then display returned results.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 70 83 90 60.5

49 44 53

49 66.5 90 99 69 75

52 47 50 50 49

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input scores: 70 83 90 60.5 average 76 grade distinction

Example 2 Input scores: 49 44 53 average 49 grade fail

Example 3 Input scores: 49 66.5 90 99 69 75 average 75 grade moderate

Example 4 Input scores: 52 47 50 50 49 average 50 grade moderate
